paper.title_en: Nonconservative Lie series: post-Newtonian binary dynamics at 2.5PN
paper.abstract_en: We develop a Lie series perturbation method for solving the dynamics of nonconservative systems within the doubled phase-space Hamiltonian framework introduced in our previous work [PRE 113, 034137]. The procedure can be applied to a wide range of perturbed nonconservative systems which are not initially given by a Hamiltonian, by casting them into the doubled phase-space where the Lie method can be employed. As an application, we tackle the non-spinning $2.5$ post-Newtonian binary problem at leading dissipative order. Starting from the ADM radiation-reaction dynamics, we construct a resonant Birkhoff normal-form and the corresponding generator of the canonical transformation. Next, we establish an analytical perturbative solution accounting for both the long-term (secular) and short-term (oscillatory) temporal behavior, without performing a small-eccentricity expansion, for nondegenerate bound eccentric orbits. The secular piece is encoded in a resonant normal-form, and captures the long-term inspiral, reconstructing exactly the known Peters-Mathews relations for semi-major axis and eccentricity. The oscillatory piece completes the dynamics by supplying instantaneous, non-averaged corrections to the orbital parameters. Combined, the two pieces give a controlled, fully canonical description of the dissipative dynamics.
